question: Should OpenClaw core adopt this startup-only ordered configuration-layer contract, including first-layer ownership, restart-only updates, and disabled mutation/reload?
rationale: This adds a public CLI and configuration lifecycle mode with long-term compatibility and operator consequences; source correctness alone cannot decide whether core should own that contract while the related RFC remains open.

options.title: Defer for RFC approval
options.body: Keep the PR open but do not merge until the managed-configuration RFC confirms the permanent core contract and owner boundaries.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow core mode
options.body: Explicitly accept the startup-only design, then require the scoped write guard and upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Keep composition external
options.body: Retain ordinary single-config OpenClaw behavior and have Lobster or another launcher materialize the effective canonical configuration before startup.

recommendation.title: Defer for RFC approval
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open but do not merge until the managed-configuration RFC confirms the permanent core contract and owner boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: The available ownership and merge history most strongly connects steipete to repository-wide configuration and Gateway contract decisions.
